A tall chimney fell with an alarming noise at Kingsclere, in Kennedy Road, carrying with it all the roof over three rooms on the top floor and part of the walls.

Another serious collapse was at the offices of the King's Buildings after a chimney broke in the roof and forced its way through four floors. The place was completely wrecked, but fortunately there was no loss of life. The upper floor, occupied by Messrs. Jebsen and Company, collapsed, and the whole floor fell through into Meyer and Company's office, with the accumulation descending into the lower floor office of the Pacific Mail Steamship Company.

Queen's College also had its roof of the assembly hall partly carried away, with their center wooden beams being thrown away like matches. The roof of their north-west classrooms were severely damaged.

Weakening further to EF1 strength, the tornado damaged trees and tore part of the roof from a home along Southeast 27th Street.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: 300-foot cell tower toppled; several homes sustained partial to total roof loss; outbuildings were damaged
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Additional EF2 damage occurred as the tornado continued along Fairground Road and began to enter the northern part of Celina. A 300-foot cell tower was toppled to the ground, several homes sustained partial to total roof loss, outbuildings and power poles were damaged, and a large swath of trees was flattened as the tornado moved through a wooded area.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: numerous homes sustained EF3 damage; one anchor-bolted house was swept clean from its foundation
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: As the storm entered a subdivision in northern Celina, it reached its peak intensity as numerous homes sustained EF3 damage. Many well-built homes in this area had their roofs ripped off and sustained collapse of numerous exterior walls. One man was killed in his home when an airborne vehicle smashed through the walls of his house. The most intense point of damage was noted at one anchor-bolted house in this area that was swept clean from its foundation and scattered through an adjacent field. Damage of this severity is typically rated at least EF4, though damage surveyors noted that the home's poorly built block foundation actually came apart underneath the bolts, rendering them ineffective. A maximum rating of EF3 was applied as a result.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: at least two-dozen homes had their roofs torn off, with some sustained collapse of exterior walls
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: The tornado maintained EF3 intensity as it continued across Touvelle Road and Jill Avenue, where at least two-dozen homes had their roofs torn off, some of which sustained collapse of exterior walls. Debris patterns in this area indicated that the tornado had a multiple-vortex structure at this point.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: The second tornado (rated EF1) touched down shortly before 0300 UTC in Nebraska, causing substantial damage to a farm and feed yard. Cars and trucks were flipped off of highways, power poles and trees were snapped, and many buildings were damaged.[28]

That evening, a damaging EF2 tornado touched down in the St. Louis suburb of Hazelwood, Missouri, tearing the roofs off of several homes and apartment buildings, downing numerous trees and power lines, and flipping many cars.[30][31]

Another EF2 tornado touched down in Van Buren County, Arkansas, prompting a tornado emergency. Significant damage was reported near Scotland, including many vehicles thrown off the road and many homes and other buildings being destroyed.[30][31]
The supercell that spawned the Scotland area tornado also produced a damaging EF2 near Mt. Olive as well.[30][31]

On April 11, a large wedge tornado touched down in Kemper County and moved into Noxubee County and Pickens County, Alabama. The tornado was rated EF3 and was on the ground for 68.4 miles. Several homes, a metal tower structure, and a steel-frame building were destroyed by the tornado.[32][33]

Later that evening, an EF2 tornado passed west of Notasulga, Alabama and heavily damaged several homes and mobile homes. One mobile home was completely destroyed, and a well-built house received major damage to an outer wall and lost its entire roof. Trees and headstones were knocked over, and one person was injured by flying glass.[37]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: The day started with a brief EF0 tornado that touched down near Kerang, causing minimal damage.
Later that day, a powerful EF3 tornado caused significant damage near the rural community of Tamleugh North; a few homes were damaged, one of which sustained major structural damage.
After the Tamleugh North tornado lifted, the most intense and long‐tracked tornado touched down in the town of Koonoomoo, tearing roofs off homes and businesses and snapping numerous trees.
The tornado reached its peak intensity of EF4 as it passed near Mulwala; a small hut was swept clean from its foundation and ground scouring was observed.
The Denison County Caravan Park sustained major damage along the tornado's path, with numerous caravans being damaged, thrown, or destroyed.
Past the caravan park, the tornado continued toward Bundalong and weakened slightly, though remained strong as a well-built brick home sustained total roof and exterior wall loss.
Maintaining its strength, the tornado then impacted the Bundalong area and significantly damaged multiple homes, some of which also sustained roof and exterior wall loss.
Later that evening, an EF0 tornado caused minor damage near Benalla.
The final tornado of the day was an EF1 that struck downtown Rutherglen, where windows were broken, awnings were ripped off, and one business sustained total collapse of a masonry exterior wall.

A large EF3 wedge tornado destroyed homes near Conway Springs.
Another large EF3 wedge tornado touched down and caused major damage in the southeastern part of Wichita.
Two EF3 wedge tornadoes passed near Fellsburg and Hudson, causing significant damage.
Multiple homes and businesses were destroyed in Woodward, Oklahoma.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Damage in Haysville ranged from EF0 to EF1 in intensity as homes sustained damage to roofs, windows, and garage doors. Trees were also downed, some of which landed on houses.

The tornado reached EF3 intensity as it entered Wichita, tearing directly through the Oaklawn-Sunview neighborhood. Major damage occurred in this residential area, as numerous one-story homes were severely damaged or destroyed, including many that lost roofs and exterior walls. One home was leveled, and many large trees were snapped, defoliated, and denuded.
Some of the most significant damage occurred at the Pinaire Mobile Home Park, where 90 of the 150 mobile homes were damaged, several of which were completely destroyed.
At nearby McConnell Air Force Base, hangars and fences were heavily damaged, and airplanes were damaged at the Kansas Aviation Museum.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: After touching down 3 miles northeast of Arnett in southern Ellis County, the tornado rapidly intensified and continued through sparsely populated areas, destroying two homes and causing lesser damage to a few others. Damage along this segment was rated EF3.
The tornado tracked northeastward into Woodward County around 11:59 p.m. CDT, producing EF2 damage. Power lines were downed and two mobile homes were completely destroyed to the southeast of Fargo.

Illuminated by lightning, the tornado entered southwestern Woodward at 12:19 a.m. CDT on April 15. It impacted a subdivision along Quail Drive and Meadowlake Drive with EF3 damage, proceeded through neighborhoods west of 34th Street and along Lakeside Lane, and later struck the Hideaway Mobile Home Park along 26th Street. In total, 89 homes and 13 businesses were reportedly damaged or destroyed in Woodward, with 10 houses leveled.

Time_Annotation: It had no official bounds; it ran year-round in 1964, but most tropical cyclones tend to form in the northwestern Pacific Ocean between June and December. These dates conventionally delimit the period of each year when most tropical cyclones form in the northwestern Pacific Ocean.
Administrative_Areas_Annotation: Notable storms include Typhoon Joan, which killed 7,000 people in Vietnam; Typhoon Louise, which killed 570 people in the Philippines; storms affecting Shanghai, China; and Typhoon Ruby, which hit Hong Kong as a powerful Category 4 storm.
Main_Event_Annotation: The 1964 Pacific typhoon season was described as the most active tropical cyclone season recorded globally, with Tropical Storms forming in the entire West Pacific basin being named.
Hazards_Annotation: The text notes catastrophic flooding in Vietnam from Typhoon Joan and extremely high wind speeds (with 1‐minute sustained speeds of 195 mph) in Typhoons Sally and Opal, as well as the destructive force of Typhoon Ruby.

Total_Summary_Deaths.Total_Deaths_Annotation: Six typhoons and two tropical storms struck Vietnam, including three tropical cyclones in a twelve-day period in November. The combined effects of Iris and Joan killed as many as 7,000 people and led to the worst floods in six decades.

Time_Annotation: The article notes that 'All months between and including May and November were featured an above-average number of typhoons relative to the 1959–1976 period' and mentions that in May 1964 conditions were favorable for tropical cyclogenesis.
Administrative_Areas_Annotation: The text states that 'More storms passed near Hong Kong in 1964 than in any prior year', 'Ten typhoons impacted the Philippines', and 'Six typhoons and two tropical storms struck Vietnam, including three tropical cyclones in a twelve-day period in November' which led to severe flooding.
Main_Event_Annotation: The description of the season—with its record number of typhoons and tropical storms—indicates that the event falls under the Tropical Storm/Cyclone category.
Hazards_Annotation: Evidence for hazards includes the issuance of tropical cyclone warning signals by the Royal Observatory Hong Kong (implying strong winds) and the report that the combined effects of Iris and Joan led to 'the worst floods in six decades' in Vietnam.

Administrative_Areas_Annotation: The text mentions multiple locations: it made landfall in Calabarzon and passed over Manila in the Philippines, hit Hainan (China) at landfall southwest of Wenchang, and finally made landfall near Haiphong, Vietnam while also tracking across northern Vietnam and southwest China.
Main_Event_Annotation: The article describes Winnie reaching tropical storm strength on June 27 and then typhoon strength on June 28 as it intensified en route to southern Luzon, which places it in the Tropical Storm/Cyclone category.

Time_Annotation: The article states, 'On June 26, a disturbance formed from an easterly tropical wave southeast of Guam and strengthened into a tropical depression later that day.' Time_Annotation: The article states: 'The disturbance that led to Typhoon Betty was first detected in the Philippine Sea on July 1 by the JTWC.' It then notes that 'the disturbance quickly developed into a tropical cyclone and strengthened into a typhoon by the end of July 2.' Further time references include 'on July 3 its winds reached 185 km/h', 'bringing its eye across southern portions of Miyakojima on July 4', 'with its sustained winds reaching 205 km/h on July 5', and finally, 'on July 6 [it] degenerated into a tropical storm and further into a tropical depression' before it 'transitioned into an extratropical cyclone on July 7 and dissipated over open waters.'
Administrative_Areas_Annotation: The text mentions that Betty took a northwestward trajectory towards the southern Ryukyu Islands and passed over Miyakojima (Japan), was located approximately 320 km south of Shanghai (China), and ultimately dissipated just off the coast of northwestern South Korea.
Main_Event_Annotation: The narrative details how the disturbance developed into a tropical cyclone and strengthened into a typhoon, which fits the 'Tropical Storm/Cyclone' category according to the provided association table.
Hazards_Annotation: Multiple sentences note extreme wind speeds – for example, 'on July 3 its winds reached 185 km/h' and 'on July 5 sustained winds reached 205 km/h' – indicating that wind is the primary hazard associated with this event.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: CNN Center was severely damaged, with shattered windows; later the glass roof of its atrium was damaged causing flooding in part of the food court, and blown-out windows in the CNN.com newsroom and videotape library contributed to minor damage.
The Georgia World Congress Center sustained serious structural damage and later experienced flooding while hosting a JROTC event and the Hinman Dental Meeting.
The Omni Hotel sustained damage, notably to its skywalk between the two hotel towers over Andrew Young International Boulevard.

The Georgia Dome had its facades damaged while hosting basketball games and, when the tornado hit, panels were ripped from its exterior with holes torn in the roof, causing insulation to fall and the scoreboard and catwalks to sway.
A Philips Arena parking garage had its facade damaged while hosting basketball games.
At the nearby Philips Arena, damage occurred to the exterior of the arena though attendees noticed little disruption during the game.
The Ritz Carlton had windows blown out.
The Westin Peachtree Plaza experienced blown-out windows that continued falling for days, leading to the closure of several city blocks and the nearby MARTA Peachtree Center station.
The Georgia-Pacific Building had windows blown out.
At SunTrust Plaza, windows were blown out, which led to more than 60 people being relocated out of their offices.
The Equitable Building had windows blown out with an annotation noting '300 at Equitable alone.'
Georgia State University experienced blown-out windows and its historic Rialto Theatre sustained roof damage, leading to interior water damage.
The Tabernacle, a former church now serving as a concert venue, suffered from blown-out windows.
Grady Hospital reported damage to windows along with a power outage.
The King Memorial MARTA station was damaged, leading to bypassing of trains and rerouted buses.
Oakland Cemetery suffered major damage to monuments as well as to its large oaks and magnolias, with window blinds even found around the neck of a statue.
A brick loft building in the Cabbagetown area lost part of its roof and a portion of its top (fifth) floor.
A building at The Stacks on Boulevard was damaged; although search and rescue personnel had difficulty entering, management confirmed that everyone was accounted for.

Administrative_Areas_Annotation: The text mentions, 'The cyclone gradually moved north-west over the next few days towards the eastern coast of India' and later 'before making landfall near Bapatla in Andhra Pradesh on December 5,' indicating India is the affected country.

Hazards_Annotation: The text reports that 'the storm peaked with sustained winds of 60 knots (110 km/h; 70 mph)' indicating high winds, and it also caused 'heavy rainfall in north-eastern Tamil Nadu including Chennai and south-eastern Andhra Pradesh,' pointing to flooding hazards.

Time_Annotation: In late November 2023, a low-pressure area crossed into the Bay of Bengal from the Gulf of Thailand; On December 1, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) reported that the disturbance had developed into a depression in the South Andaman Sea; On December 2, the system intensified into a deep depression about 440 kilometres east-southeast of Puducherry; On December 4, cyclone Michaung reached peak intensity as it approached the coast of Tamil Nadu; On December 5, the storm made landfall between Nellore and Machilipatnam in Andhra Pradesh; By December 6, the storm had weakened to a depression over central Andhra Pradesh.
Administrative_Areas_Annotation: The impact is evident from the involvement of the India Meteorological Department, the approach of the cyclone towards Tamil Nadu, and its landfall in Andhra Pradesh, all of which indicate that India was affected.
Main_Event_Annotation: The report mentions that the system intensified into a cyclonic storm and later reached peak intensity as cyclone Michaung, which aligns with the Tropical Storm/Cyclone category.
Hazards_Annotation: The storm is associated with strong winds, as evidenced by cyclone Michaung reaching peak intensity with winds of 110 kilometres per hour.
